_comment: spec-v7 Step 123 — mutation testing. Scoped to the highest-value pure extractors plus the pre-disclosure pack's scanner and masking helpers (`src/delivery/sensitive.ts`, `src/delivery/mask.ts`), whose failure direction is the worst in the tree — a false NEGATIVE that reports a document clean, or a mask that does not mask; a separate, slow, on-demand/scheduled job, never the per-push gate. `mutate` here and the `include` list in vitest.mutation.config.ts MUST describe the same surface: `include` needs EVERY test file that imports a mutated module, not just the same-named one — a module whose sibling phrasing suite is left out has its kills go uncounted and reports them as NoCoverage. tests/integration/mutation-scope.test.ts derives the correct include list from the test files' own imports and asserts this config matches.
_thresholds_comment: Regression-only (spec-v7 Step 124): break a couple points under the measured baseline; never an aspiration. Runs only in the scheduled/on-demand mutation workflow, not the per-push gate. Ratchet up as survivors are killed. SUPERSEDED baseline 56.92% over amounts+crossrefs+dates+jurisdictions+obligations+parties+sections+delivery/sensitive (4,317 mutants), 2026-09-07, break 54. NOTE scores are comparable ONLY within one `mutate` set AND one include list. History: 51.26% baseline (2026-06-05, dates+amounts, break 48); decayed to 47.59 and BROKE the gate; covering then-untested features took the pair to 56.16; scope widened to four files (52.34); pinning each external-citation branch in crossrefs took it to 53.94; then the include list was corrected to name every covering test file (several phrasing suites had never run under mutation, so their kills went uncounted) and the scope widened to seven files → 55.51; pinning the three governing-law clause-tail helpers and the party phantom/signature cases → 56.94. CEILING NOTE: crossrefs' ~270 remaining survivors are mostly EQUIVALENT mutants inside long alternations (\s+ -> \s, [A-Za-z]+ -> [A-Za-z], dropped ^ anchors) that no realistic legal drafting distinguishes — 41 new branch-pinning test rows moved it only 42.86 -> 46.80. Further gains need a different lever, not more rows. 2026-09-07: scope widened to the PRE-DISCLOSURE SCANNER (src/delivery/sensitive.ts, 66.15% on its own 195 mutants) because two of its tests were caught passing with the scanner stubbed to return nothing — the class this whole job exists to find. Aggregate barely moved (56.94 -> 56.92) because the module scores above the mean and the extractors grew 2,696 -> 4,122 mutants of their own in the same period; per-file percentages are NOT comparable across those two runs. 2026-09-08: scope widened again to src/delivery/mask.ts (88.24% on its own 102 mutants after its safety paths were pinned, 80.39% before) — the module that decides WHAT GETS MASKED, and luhnValid's length window, which is the false-positive control for card numbers. Above the mean, so break 54 was unaffected. 2026-09-08: the full run finally happened — **59.66%** over the ten-module scope (3,249 killed / 2,153 survived / 106 timeout / 116 no-coverage), so `break` moves 54 → 57. It took 61 minutes and logged 79 test-runner OOM restarts against the workflow's 120-minute timeout; the score is real and the margin is thin. See docs/v7/mutation-baseline.md. 2026-09-08: scope widened to src/report/critical-dates.ts — the DEADLINE ARITHMETIC, whose failure direction is an attorney acting on a wrong date. It measured 44.02% on its own 502 mutants, BELOW the aggregate, so it was not eligible; 55 of those mutants had no test executing them at all, including the backward-counted-period branch whose comment records an audit bug (Math.abs flipped the direction and moved the answer 2N days late) and the FRCP 6(d) service-days path. Pinning those took it to 57.17%, above the aggregate, which is what made widening safe. Same day, src/report/exports.ts — the fix list, obligations CSV and deadlines calendar, the artifacts a reviewer WORKS FROM — went 46.08% → 58.53% over four releases and joined too. It started BELOW the aggregate and was recorded in the baseline doc as ineligible rather than guessed at; what raised it was its 100 NoCoverage mutants, which named the ten *Blob wrappers (the browser's actual download path, tested by nothing), every "verify manually" reason the calendar gives for a deadline it could not pin, the asserted-pack receipts and input-warning banners in the fix-list header, and the citation staleness label. Two of the new tests were caught VACUOUS before landing — one dropped the anchor definition and so never reached the branch at all, and the responsible-party suite asserted only `not.toBe(<wrong name>)`, which every mutant satisfies.
